subject: Ramp-to-commit proposal and wallet redemption cadence
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Ramp-to-commit proposal and wallet redemption cadence

Hi Sarah —

Thanks for taking time last week. Per our conversation I put together a concise framing for a multi-year committed spend with a staged drawdown (annual wallets) and a redemption cadence. Attached is a short term summary (Redwood_Term_Summary.xlsx) and a draft SOW to align on onboarding scope.

Key starting point I want your feedback on:
- Total commitment: $2.4M over 3 years (annual wallets of $900k / $800k / $700k as illustrative)
- Redemption cadence: quarterly drawdowns from each annual wallet (teams draw credits monthly, we true-up monthly)
- Ramp protection: front-loaded credits for year 1 to absorb early burst; year-over-year taper
- Early termination & refunds: pro rata minus service consumption + 1-quarter escrow hold

Questions for you:
1) Does Acme prefer a single prepay invoice (upfront) or annual invoices tied to wallet start dates?
2) Do you need an escrowed buffer or would a 30-day invoice hold be sufficient for finance?
3) Any constraints on audit rights / usage logs for compliance?

If this framing looks reasonable I can loop in Karthik and Marissa to finalize discount tiers and an explicit drawdown table.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0183

Attachments: Redwood_Term_Summary.xlsx (spreadsheet - pricing/term bullets), Draft_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW stub)

From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acme.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ramp-to-commit proposal and wallet redemption cadence

Thanks Jordan — helpful framing. A few immediate items from procurement and finance:

- Invoice cadence: Finance prefers annual invoicing aligned to our fiscal year, but we can do an upfront prepay if necessary; need to know refund mechanics.
- Amortization: We will amortize the prepay against usage monthly. Need a sample amortization schedule and the contract language that governs it.
- Escrow/hold: Our FP&A team wants a 60-day buffer rather than 30 days if we’re front-loading credits in year 1. They want to avoid paying out for credits that don’t get used in Q1.
- Audit & logs: SOC2 evidence and per-customer usage logs are required — can Redwood provide token- or request-level logs for the past 12 months?

Also — pricing question: Acme’s procurement is asking for a more predictable blended discount rather than a complicated year-by-year schedule. If you can propose a blended rate as an alternative that maps to the $2.4M commitment, that will make approvals faster.

Can you share the amortization example and a proposed blended discount?

Thanks,
Sarah Liu
Vendor Strategy & Procurement, Acme, Inc.

--
Sarah sent this from her mobile

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Ramp-to-commit proposal and wallet redemption cadence

Team — forwarding Acme's responses. Procurement is signaling they want: annual invoicing OR an upfront prepay but with a clearer refund/amortization clause and a 60-day buffer on front-loaded credits. They also want a blended discount option.

I think a commercially simple option that we can offer quickly:
- Option A (standard): Upfront 3-year prepay $2.4M, annual wallets, quarterly drawdown, discounts tiered (Y1>Y2>Y3). 1-quarter escrow to cover early churn. Monthly usage true-up.
- Option B (procurement-friendly): Annual invoicing (3 invoices), blended discount across term (single %), explicit monthly amortization schedule, 60-day buffer on credits.

Can you:
- Karthik: draft a blended discount % that is economics-equivalent to a tiered schedule but looks simpler to finance. Include brief ARR math and gross margin impact.
- Marissa: confirm whether SOC2/usage logs and the 60-day buffer are acceptable from an operational standpoint.
- Rishi: flag any legal hotspots for the early termination pro rata refund + escrow language.

I attached a quick pricing impact export (pricing_impact_analysis.csv) — please update and return by EOD so I can respond to Acme.

Thanks,
Jordan

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Ramp-to-commit proposal and wallet redemption cadence

Jordan / team — see proposed commercial framing below. I ran a quick model against the $2.4M base case and included suggested legal/ops guardrails.

Proposed commercial structure (recommended):
- Term: 3 years, total committed prepay $2.4M (billing option selectable: upfront or annual invoices)
- Wallet split (recommendation): Year1 $960k (40%), Year2 $720k (30%), Year3 $720k (30%) — this favors initial runway for their expected pilot bursts.
- Redemption cadence: monthly consumption with quarterly checkpoints and monthly true-up.
- Discounting: instead of tiered 15/10/5, offer two consumer-facing choices:
  - Tiered (clear savings profile): Year1 15% / Year2 10% / Year3 5% (blended ~10.5%)
  - Blended (procurement-friendly): single 12% off list for the entire committed spend (economics close to blended tiering, simplifies PO).
- Escrow / buffer: propose 1-quarter escrow funded from the first invoice (equal to 25% of Year1 wallet) with explicit release mechanics tied to usage thresholds. For buyers insisting on 60-day hold, we can extend to 60 days but require an offset (1% less discount).
- Early termination: pro rata refund of unused wallet minus consumed services and final true-up; refund timeline 90 days after termination request; standard fees for migration/legal.
- Overuse: standard pay-as-you-go overage rates at list (monthly invoiced); recommend capped overage tier for first 6 months.

Commercial rationale: the blended 12% option moves approvals quicker while preserving ~80-90% of our margin benefit vs the tiered schedule. Escrow protects against aggressive early-burn scenarios and gives finance visibility.

Legal/ops notes (high level):
- Rishi: suggest we make the escrow releasable upon three consecutive months where usage reaches >= 70% of the then-available wallet; also call out that logs and request-level events will be available for audit with a standard non-prod window for PII redaction.
- Marissa: confirm if the ops team can support a 60-day buffer and the release triggers without manual work.

I attached a quick calc and the draft redlines (commit_terms_redlines.docx). Happy to sharpen numbers — tell me if CFO wants a different blended target.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_impact_analysis.csv, commit_terms_redlines.docx

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@acme.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, procurement@acme.com
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 15:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Ramp-to-commit proposal and wallet redemption cadence

Sarah — thanks and appreciate the clarity from procurement. Quick summary and next steps: 

We can support both commercial paths you outlined. Two firm options we recommend for your review:

1) Blended-simplicity (fast-approve): 3-year commit $2.4M, annual invoicing, 12% blended discount, monthly amortization, 60-day buffer on front-loaded credits (as you requested). No escrow; blended discount offsets buffer impact.

2) Upside-protect (preferred economic outcome): Upfront prepay $2.4M, wallet split Y1/Y2/Y3 as 40/30/30, tiered discount (15/10/5), 1-quarter escrow funded from first invoice with release tied to usage thresholds, monthly true-up, pro rata refund on termination with 90-day payout.

Operational points: we provide per-request usage logs and can include a SOC2 attestation package in the contract. Overages billed monthly; we can offer a capped overage rate for first 6 months.

Next steps that will keep approvals moving:
- Choose Option 1 or 2 and confirm preferred billing cadence (upfront vs annual invoices).
- If Option 1: we’ll issue a purchase-ready summary (one-page) with blended discount and amortization schedule for your finance team.
- If Option 2: we’ll circulate the SOW + redlines and escrow mechanics; legal will propose specific escrow release language.

I’ve attached a one-pager and the draft SOW for your review. Can we set a 30-minute call Thursday to lock a path? If procurement approves a blended 12% today we can route a PO for signatures and target an April start.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced above: Redwood_Term_Summary.xlsx (updated), Draft_SOW_v3.pdf (updated)
